A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same ReaDISH study. Their main text, equations, figures, tables, checklist, and Appendices A–J are available and readable, supporting a reliable comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original ReaDISH benchmark evaluations, permutation experiments, component ablations, and training-size analyses in Section 4 and Appendices E–H.

after.justification: v3 retains these original empirical results, including benchmark comparisons, robustness tests, ablations, and appendix analyses.

M1.justification: The architecture, shingle construction and pooling, interaction-aware attention, and pretraining objective are unchanged. The revised abstract's description of continuous embeddings extending DRFP describes the existing method, not a new component.

E1.justification: Both use the same USPTO/CJHIF pretraining data and seven downstream datasets covering yield, enantioselectivity, conversion, and reaction-type prediction. Random and out-of-sample scenarios remain unchanged (Section 4.1, Appendix B).

E2.justification: The comparisons retain YieldBERT, YieldBERT-DA, UA-GNN, UAM, and ReaMVP, plus the cross-attention baseline in Appendix E, Table 4. The more prominent DRFP attribution does not introduce an evaluated comparator.

E3.justification: Split definitions and sample counts in Table 3, evaluation metrics in Section 4.1, training settings in Tables 5–6, and baseline evaluation procedures in Appendix F are unchanged.

E4.justification: Both retain the same permutation tests, component and shingle-radius ablations, shingle-count distributions, clustering analysis, and training-size study. No analyses or supporting evidence are added or removed.

E5.justification: Both report five permutation runs in Section 4.2 and ten random splits plus five out-of-sample random runs in Appendix F. Uncertainty-reporting practices are unchanged; no statistical tests or additional run information are introduced.

E6.justification: Numerical results and qualitative findings are unchanged throughout the main text and appendices. For example, Table 1 retains ReaDISH R2 values of 0.480 ± 0.032 for BH and 0.549 ± 0.019 for SM; Tables 2, 4, and 7–9 also retain their results.

T1.justification: Equations 1–12 and Algorithm 1 retain the same definitions, mathematical constructions, attention formulation, and training objective. No assumptions, derivations, or proofs are added or revised.

C1.justification: The abstract refines the first innovation as extending DRFP through continuous high-dimensional shingle embeddings, and the introduction explicitly says the symmetric difference is adopted from DRFP. This qualifies the novelty framing; the interaction-modeling and performance claims remain unchanged.

C2.justification: Interpretations of permutation robustness, ablation effects, ELN generalization difficulties, and training-size trends are unchanged. Appendix I retains the same computational-overhead limitation and proposed mitigation.

D1.justification: Appendices B–F retain the same preprocessing, conformer generation, shingle limits, hyperparameters, hardware, and runtime disclosures. The documented code-availability statement and repository link are unchanged.

R1.justification: v3 explicitly foregrounds DRFP as the source of symmetric-difference shingles in the abstract and introduction. v1 already cited and discussed DRFP in Section 3.2 and Appendix A, so this is a limited attribution and positioning refinement. The set of cited works is unchanged.

P1.justification: There are localized abstract and introduction edits, updated affiliations naming the AGI Institute and Shanghai Innovation Institute, and corresponding citation renumbering. The section organization and remaining narrative are preserved.

P2.justification: The expanded affiliation block and revised line wrapping reflow the abstract and introduction across the first two pages. Figures and tables retain their content, captions, structure, and placement.

improvement.justification: Explicit DRFP attribution in the abstract and introduction clarifies the contribution boundary and aligns the opening claims with the relationship already explained in v1's Appendix A. This provides a limited improvement in attribution and clarity; the method, empirical evidence, limitations, and reproducibility information remain unchanged.
